pr_title: Use HashCode.Combine() in interop source generators and analyzers instead of custom GetHashCode implementations
pr_body:
Use the HashCode.Combine from shared Roslyn code rather than use the custom implementations that xor the values together. This PR fixes all overrides of GetHashCode in System.Runtime.InteropServices.

fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/86104

issue_context.title: Interop source generators and analyzers should use HashCode.Combine to implement GetHashCode
issue_context.body: Overrides of GetHashCode that try to combine the hash codes of fields/properties should use HashCode.Combine() instead of custom implementations.
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/interop-contrib See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
Overrides of GetHashCode that try to combine the hash codes of fields/properties should use HashCode.Combine() instead of the custom implementations that are used currently. HashCode doesn't exist in the framework libraries in netstandard2.0, but there is a nuget package that provides the same functionality. https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Bcl.HashCode
Author: jtschuster
Assignees: jtschuster
Labels: `area-System.Runtime.InteropServices`
Milestone: -

review_comments:
Maybe I'm missing something crucial here, but how does hashcode resolve to shared roslyn code here?
Don't you need to manually include some shared Codebase sourcefile?
Ah, one of the ugly hacks, srcGens in this repo can use to make the code more readable. Everyone else trying this will run into the .NET Standard 2.0 brick wall.
Others can use the `Microsoft.Bcl.HashCode` package (with some difficulty sadly around referencing NuGet packages in source generators). We have reasons why we can't easily use that here.
